index.pageTitle: XcodeSentinel — Keep Your Xcode Claude Sessions Running
index.pageDescription: A free macOS menu-bar app that watches the Claude coding session inside Xcode and resumes it automatically when it stalls — so it isn't left idle for hours while you're away.
index.heroLead: Step away from your Mac and come back to a finished build, not a frozen Claude session. XcodeSentinel watches your Xcode windows and resumes automatically.
index.heroMeta: macOS 15 or later · Developer ID signed · Notarized · Free
index.downloadSubtitle: Free, open source, and signed with a Developer ID.
index.downloadMeta: macOS 15+ · Developer ID signed & notarized · Free
index.problemBody:
You have Claude writing code inside Xcode, step away for a meeting or go to sleep — and come back hours later to find it stopped cold:

  • The 5-hour rolling usage limit was hit while you were away.
  • The weekly limit cut in and requires a long wait.
  • Output was long and Claude is waiting on "Continue".

You don't notice until it's too late, and it stays stopped even after the limit resets on its own.
index.solutionBody:
XcodeSentinel runs silently in your menu bar and polls each registered Xcode window's Claude panel via the Accessibility API — no screenshots, no OCR, no extra permissions.

  • When a limit clears, it resumes your own session — one window at a time, paced, in priority order.
  • Notifies you on macOS and optionally via webhook (ntfy, Pushover, Discord, Slack) so you can see what happened from your phone.
  • If it can't determine the state, it notifies you and does nothing — it never sends into an unknown state.
index.featuresBody:
🔍Smart state detection

Eight distinct states: idle / working / awaiting-continue / session-limited / weekly-limited / awaiting-approval / awaiting-answer / errored. Driven by editable Patterns.json — update without rebuilding.

🛡️Safe auto-resume

One retry per stall, a daily cap (default 12), cooldowns, and a Dry-run mode that detects but never sends. Zero action on unknown or approval states.

📋Resume scheduler

Priority queue — one window at a time by default (up to 3). 90-second spacing between starts. Configurable Quiet Hours window.

📲Away notifications

Generic webhook with ntfy / Pushover / Discord / Slack presets. Sends only the target name, state, and timestamp — never chat text or source code.

🔬AX Inspector

Dump any window's Accessibility tree to JSON for bug reports and regression tests. Export and attach to GitHub Issues when Xcode updates break detection.

⚡Lightweight

Menu-bar only app, no Dock icon. Pure Swift 6, no external dependencies. Accessibility API only — no Screen Recording permission needed.

howToInstallSteps.title: Download the DMG
howToInstallSteps.body: Grab the latest .dmg from GitHub Releases. Double-click to mount it.

howToInstallSteps.title: Drag to Applications
howToInstallSteps.body: Drag XcodeSentinel into your Applications folder. Launch it — it lives in the menu bar.

howToInstallSteps.title: Grant Accessibility permission
howToInstallSteps.body: On first run, it opens System Settings → Privacy → Accessibility. Enable it there. No Screen Recording needed.

gettingStarted.pageDescription: Install XcodeSentinel and register your first Xcode target in five minutes.
gettingStarted.heading: Getting Started
gettingStarted.headingLead: From download to your first monitored session in about 5 minutes.
gettingStarted.installBody:
1. Download the latest .dmg from GitHub Releases.
  2. Open the DMG and drag XcodeSentinel to your Applications folder.
  3. Launch it. It appears in the menu bar (no Dock icon).
gettingStarted.gatekeeperBody: The build is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so a normal double-click works. If macOS still blocks it, right-click the app in Finder → Open → Open once. You only need to do this once.
gettingStarted.permissionBody: On first run the app asks for Accessibility permission and opens System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Enable XcodeSentinel there. Screen Recording is not requested — XcodeSentinel reads Accessibility attributes only, never pixel content.
gettingStarted.targetBody:
1. Click the menu bar icon → Settings → Targets → Add Target…
  2. Pick a running Xcode window from the list (identified by workspace name).
  3. Give it a display name and a resume prompt. Default: "Please continue from where you stopped."
  4. Press Test Detection — confirm the Claude panel is found before you rely on automation.
gettingStarted.dryRunBody: For the first day or two, keep Dry-run on (Settings → Scheduler). Detection runs normally but nothing is sent — the log shows what would have been sent. Disable it once you trust the detection results.
gettingStarted.screenshotsNote: Screenshots will be added with the first tagged release.

guide.pageDescription: All features: targets, detection patterns, the scheduler, Quiet Hours, and webhook notifications.
guide.heading: Guide
guide.headingLead: Everything you need to know about configuring and using XcodeSentinel.
guide.targetsBody:
A target is one monitored Xcode window. It is stored by workspace path and display name, and re-bound to a live window on each app launch (restarting Xcode changes its PID). Per-target settings:

  • Priority — lower number runs first in the resume queue
  • Resume prompt — what gets sent (default:

)
  • Daily auto-resume cap — default 12
  • Minimum interval between resumes — default 120 s
  • Notify on stall
  • Require manual approval for destructive stops
guide.detectionBody: State is read from Accessibility text and matched against rules in Patterns.json (editable in Settings → Detection, no rebuild needed). Each rule has anyOf / allOf / noneOf substring lists, an optional role constraint, and an enabled flag. The first matching rule wins, so specific rules (weekly limit) should precede general ones (session limit). Test Detection shows the resolved state and any rules that nearly matched — use it after every Xcode update.
guide.schedulerBody:
Targets that become resume-eligible are queued, not run immediately. The queue is ordered by priority, then by how long the target has been stalled. Defaults:

  • One resume in flight at a time (configurable up to 3)
  • 90 seconds between queue dispatches
  • Limit states are held until their published reset time before dispatch
guide.quietHoursBody: Set a daily window (e.g. 23:00–07:00) during which the app notifies but never sends. Windows that cross midnight are handled correctly. Useful when you're actually asleep and prefer not to resume.
guide.safetyBody:
• One automatic resume per stall; a second only if the stall recurs for the same reason; stop and notify on the third.
  • Daily cap per target (default 12). Resets at midnight.
  • Cooldown between resumes (default 120 s).
  • No auto-response to awaitingApproval or awaitingUserAnswer — notify only.
  • No action on unknown or errored states.
  • Dry-run: detect only, never send.
guide.webhookBody: Set an endpoint URL and pick a preset (ntfy / Pushover / Discord / Slack) or write a custom JSON template using {{title}}, {{message}}, {{timestamp}}. The payload contains only the target's display name, the state, and a timestamp — never chat text or source code.
guide.axInspectorBody: Debug → AX Inspector shows the selected window's Accessibility tree with role / title / value / identifier, highlights the currently matching pattern, and exports the tree as JSON. Attach that JSON to GitHub Issues when detection breaks after an Xcode update (check it contains no real project names or paths first).

troubleshooting.pageDescription: Detection failures, lost Accessibility permission, Xcode updates, and using the AX Inspector.
troubleshooting.heading: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.detectionBody:
1. Open Debug → AX Inspector and dump the target window's tree.
  2. If the Claude panel elements aren't visible, the panel may be a separate window — remove and re-add the target.
  3. If the text is present but the wording changed (after an Xcode update), update Patterns.json in Settings → Detection.
  4. After three consecutive "unknown" results the app pauses monitoring and sends a notification. Fix the root cause, then tap Resume monitoring.
troubleshooting.permissionBody: Re-signing the app or an OS update can silently drop the Accessibility permission. XcodeSentinel detects this and notifies you. Re-enable it under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
troubleshooting.xcodeTitle: Detection Broke After an Xcode Update
troubleshooting.xcodeBody: Xcode's Claude-panel Accessibility structure is private and can change between Xcode versions. Most cases are fixed by updating Patterns.json in Settings → Detection. If the structure itself changed, open a GitHub Issue with an AX Inspector JSON dump attached.
troubleshooting.noResumeBody: This is usually intentional. XcodeSentinel never auto-resumes on awaitingApproval, awaitingUserAnswer, unknown, or errored. For other states, check: the daily cap, the cooldown, the per-stall retry limit, Dry-run mode, and Quiet Hours.
troubleshooting.weeklyBody: The weekly limit does not reset after 5 hours — it has its own longer cycle. On weeklyLimited the app switches to a long polling interval (re-checks about every 30 minutes) and sends a notification.
troubleshooting.webhookBody: Check the endpoint URL and template in Settings → Notifications. The presets (ntfy / Pushover / Discord / Slack) fill in the required format automatically. Test by sending a test notification from the settings screen.

privacy.pageDescription: What XcodeSentinel reads, what it sends, and what it never sends.
privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.headingLead: XcodeSentinel is designed to be minimal and transparent about what it accesses.
privacy.readsBody:
Through the macOS Accessibility API, for each window you register: element roles, titles, values, and identifiers within the Claude panel hierarchy. This is how it detects session state, finds the input field, and locates the Send button.

It does not read pixel content, take screenshots, or use OCR.
privacy.sendsBody:
• Local macOS notifications: target display name, state, next action.
  • Optional webhook (only if you configure a URL): target display name, state, timestamp.
privacy.neverBody:
• Chat message contents.
  • Source code or file contents.
  • Real file paths or project names in webhook payloads.

Detailed debug logging that could include more is opt-in and off by default. Logs never record chat text under any default configuration.
privacy.permsBody:
• Accessibility — required to read panel state and send input.
  • Screen Recording — not requested. No screenshots, no OCR.
  • Notifications — requested at first run; used for local alerts only.
privacy.networkBody: No analytics, no tracking, no telemetry. The only outbound network request is the webhook you configure, sent to the URL you provide. There is no default server-side component.

faq.pageDescription: Common questions about scope, limits, App Store distribution, and safety.
faq.heading: FAQ

items.q: Does this get around the usage limit?
items.a: No. It does not bypass, extend, or work around any limit. It resumes your own session after a limit has already cleared, and it will not keep sending while a limit is active.

items.q: Why Xcode only? What about VS Code or the Claude Code CLI?
items.a: Claude Code already has an official "Continue automatically at usage limit" setting (on by default since v2.1.234), and the VS Code extension is built on Claude Code, so it inherits that. Xcode's Claude integration is an Apple IDE feature on a separate track and has no equivalent — that gap is why this app exists.

items.q: Why isn't it on the Mac App Store?
items.a: It drives another app (Xcode) through the Accessibility API, which is not possible inside the App Sandbox that the Mac App Store requires. It is distributed via GitHub Releases as a Developer ID–signed, notarized DMG.

items.q: Is it safe to run unattended?
items.a: It is built to fail safe: it never acts on an unknown state, never answers approval prompts or questions from Claude, caps retries and daily resumes per target, and has a Dry-run mode that never sends anything. Even so, review the safety settings and start in Dry-run for the first day.

items.q: Does it work for the weekly limit?
items.a: It detects the weekly limit and switches to a long polling interval. It cannot make the weekly limit reset sooner.

items.q: Does it work when my Mac screen is locked?
items.a: When the display is locked, the OS blocks keyboard event delivery to running apps. XcodeSentinel detects this state and defers any pending resumes until the screen is unlocked, then fires immediately. Monitoring (detection) continues normally while locked.

items.q: Is this made by Anthropic or Apple?
items.a: No. It is an independent open-source tool made by a solo developer. "Xcode" and "Claude" are trademarks of their respective owners.
